summary: This fable is about a thirsty crow who outsmarts a scheming fox by dropping pebbles into a jar to raise the water instead of falling for his trick.
introduce: Show the title “The Clever Fox and the Thirsty Crow” and ask, “What do you think will happen in this story, and why?” Explain that good readers use clues in the text together with what they already know to make inferences.

keyTerms.def: able to wait calmly without getting upset
having made a firm decision to keep trying
a secret plan, often meant to trick someone

challengeTerms.def: very clever and original, especially in solving a problem
to defeat someone by being smarter or more clever than them
continuing to try something despite difficulty

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that being clever and patient will always work better than trying to trick someone? Use evidence from the story to explain.
Explain why the fox's plan would not have worked, and explain how the crow's plan was better.
struggling: Pre-teach patient, determined, and scheme with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers answer “What clue tells you that?” questions using sentence starters.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use ingenious, outwit, and persistence in a short paragraph that makes an inference that the story does not state and support it with two clues.
